title: API keys
intro: API keys let you create links and check stats straight from your code, without opening the dashboard. Each key is an independent Bearer token: name it after where it will be used and revoke it when you no longer need it.

revokeDialog.title: Revoke this key?
revokeDialog.body: Integrations and scripts using this key will stop working immediately. This action cannot be undone.

empty.title: You don't have any API keys yet
empty.body: Create your first key in the form below to integrate Link Charts with your code: shorten links and track stats from any script, bot, or system.

create.heading: Create new key
create.nameHint: Just for you to identify where the key is used. Maximum of {{max}} characters.

validation.maxLength: The name can have at most {{max}} characters.

errors.limitReached: You reached the limit of {{max}} keys. Revoke an existing key to create another.
errors.rateLimited: Too many attempts in a row. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.generic: Could not create the key. Try again.

create.limitReachedNotice: You reached the limit of {{max}} API keys. Revoke an existing key to create another.

tokenDialog.title: Key created
tokenDialog.intro: This is your "{{name}}" key. Copy it and store it somewhere safe — for security, it will not be shown again.
tokenDialog.warning: Save it now: this is the only time the full key is shown. If you lose it, revoke this one and create another.

usage.heading: How to use the API
usage.intro: Every call carries the key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. With it you create short links and check click stats from anywhere: an automation script, a bot, a CRM or spreadsheet integration.
usage.keepSecret: Treat the key like a password: don't commit it to Git or expose it in code that runs in the browser.

createExample.title: Create a link
createExample.description: POST to /api/v1/links with the destination URL. The response includes the link id and the short URL. Optional: subdomain_id picks which of your custom addresses the link uses — omit the field for your default address; null forces the main domain.

statsExample.title: Check stats
statsExample.description: GET /api/v1/links/{id}/stats returns the link's clicks — use the id returned on creation.
